PullRequest.Title: automations: refactor: make provider session templates canonical

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronizer's serialized while-loop, generation update, one-second timeout, and post-await generation check are explicit in the changed code. The new test also establishes that provider capture may never settle. Exact provider stall prevalence is uncertain, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Provider configuration capture promises, including Agent Host configuration-resolution IPC, plus serialized wall-clock wait time.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is one capture/timeout per synchronization iteration rather than one per old draft; rapid target changes during a stalled capture can repeatedly pay 1,000 ms against the same session, and timed-out underlying promises remain pending.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Retarget UI latency grows by the one-second capture timeout for each stale synchronization iteration, blocking creation and display of the final target draft.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, target synchronization validated the workspace and immediately created the latest draft; it did not await provider capture or repeat stalled capture work while coalescing target changes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Retargeting now synchronously captures the previous provider draft before creating the requested draft; stale retarget iterations still pay that capture and leave the old draft installed, causing the next iteration to capture it again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `await this.captureSessionConfiguration(this.session, this.appliedTarget, this.retargetConfigurationCaptureTimeoutMs);` runs before the stale-generation check. `update()` marks another sync iteration while the await is pending, so after a timeout the stale iteration returns and the next iteration invokes the same capture again against the unchanged draft.
Findings.Title: Coalesce capture before applying the latest target
Findings.Impact: When an Agent Host/provider configuration request is slow or disconnected, quickly switching folder/provider/session type leaves the session controls unavailable for roughly two seconds for a common A→B→C correction, and further switches can add another timeout while also spawning additional never-settling capture promises.
Findings.Evidence: `scheduleSync()` serializes updates in a loop. During `sync()`, line 365 awaits capture with a 1,000 ms timeout and only then checks whether `generation` changed. For A→B followed quickly by C while A's capture stalls, B's iteration waits one second, observes it is stale, leaves A as `this.session`, and the queued C iteration waits another second capturing A again. `captureSessionConfiguration` uses `raceTimeout` without cancelling the underlying provider promise, and `automationDialog.test.ts` explicitly covers a never-resolving capture promise.
Findings.Recommendation: Coalesce capture by applied session: start at most one capture attempt for the old draft, share its result/deadline across queued target updates, and after it settles or times out create only the latest requested target. Also cancel or otherwise release the underlying provider capture when abandoning the draft.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open/edit an Automation, switch workspace/provider/session type, and save the provider-owned session template
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening or retargeting must create the selected provider draft before configuration controls become available; Save additionally waits for synchronization and a final capture. The newly added previous-target capture is on the retarget critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture provider configuration; Agent Host capture may wait for or retry `resolveSessionConfig` over the host connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one final capture on Save plus one capture per retarget synchronization iteration. With A→B→C during a stalled A capture, A is captured twice because the stale iteration leaves it applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Retargeting validated and created the latest draft without capturing the old provider draft first; Save did not perform provider-owned capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each retarget capture blocks creation and display of the next draft for up to 1,000 ms; final Save is bounded by a shared 5,000 ms deadline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider schema/configuration and eagerly create the Agent Host draft backend.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One draft initialization for the effective target after coalescing, although changing targets creates a replacement draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automation target changes already created provider drafts and initiated their configuration/backend lifecycle, but without canonical template restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration controls depend on draft creation/config resolution; this boundary already existed for Automation drafts, while the diff adds template payload and restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and timing of target changes while provider capture is pending; effective cardinality is synchronization iterations, not raw picker events. A quick A→B→C produces two captures of A when capture stalls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single serialized synchronizer processes target changes. Equal updates coalesce, but a changed generation does not cancel the in-flight capture and the next iteration can recapture the same applied draft.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The dialog caches the latest successful configuration per concrete target for its lifetime. Cache keys include target kind, folder URI, provider, and session type; there is no cross-dialog cache. Timed-out captures do not populate the cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the await precedes the generation check, synchronization is serialized, and the old draft remains applied after a stale iteration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider stalls are environment-dependent, but the tests explicitly permit a never-settling capture. The added delay is deterministically bounded at one second per stale iteration.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing latency regression; submitted one finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run an Automation through Agent Host authority or the older browser/fallback runner
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session creation and the first request are on the run critical path. Canonical model/config values are now supplied at creation; fallback custom-agent runs additionally wait for fresh agent discovery before send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the run session and start it through the Agent Host execution service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create and one start per Automation run; no per-template-field fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one create plus one start occurred, without complete canonical model metadata in the first turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both calls remain on the run startup path. The diff only adds model configuration to the existing first message/session payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/configure a fallback provider session and send the first request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session creation and one request per run; target isolation remains configured once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fallback created the same session and request, then optionally applied flat model/mode/permission setters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the fallback run can proceed. The boundary is pre-existing; the diff moves canonical template restoration into creation rather than post-create setters.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh workspace custom-agent modes before sending a fallback Automation using a custom agent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery sequence per first send, with a single 30-second deadline even if selection changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canonical custom-agent Automation templates were not supported on this fallback path, so this discovery wait was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first request until the selected agent is resolved; cancellation and timeout dispose each discovery scope.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automation run count; each run creates one fresh session. Custom-agent discovery does not fan out by automation collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs follow existing scheduler/runner concurrency. Within a fallback run, custom-agent discovery is serialized before first send and bounded by one deadline.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each run is a fresh session; model preferences come from the saved template. Custom-agent availability is deliberately revalidated rather than trusted from a stale cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call paths and bounds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider/session creation and agent-discovery duration vary, but call cardinality is fixed at one sequence per run.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: canonical restoration does not add boundary fan-out, and the new custom-agent discovery is required, single-shot, cancellable, and bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive Agent Host Automation catalog updates, list/edit definitions, and persist browser legacy-store definitions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Catalog projection feeds the Automation view and mutation conflict checks; browser-store persistence runs on create/update/import, not per frame.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive authoritative Automation catalog snapshots/actions from Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing subscription; each catalog change can reproject all N definitions and runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Catalog updates already reprojected and sorted all Automations; only model/mode/permission fields were exposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Projection occurs before consumers observe updated lists. The diff adds shallow projection of each template config but no new IPC request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stable-stringify editable state, now including the complete session template, for optimistic conflict checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A small fixed number of serializations per mutation/approval check; not per render or run-history item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same checks serialized flat fields but not the provider template.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on user/tool mutation paths. Tool-supplied opaque configuration is bounded to 65,536 serialized characters and 10,000 values.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, parse, migrate, and write the Automation ledger through the storage service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup/load parse and one write per mutation, across N Automations; schema migration maps each row once on load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The ledger already persisted all Automation rows and runs, without canonical template data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Startup/load and mutations already depended on storage; the diff increases payload by the bounded template size.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automation count N and aggregate template size. Tool input is bounded; provider-authored Agent Host config size is not established as large in normal use.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog projection and mutation checks are synchronous; storage mutations retain existing sequencing/optimistic guards.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Derived catalog observables recompute on catalog changes. Run-specific observables are cached by automation ID; template projection itself is not memoized.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added serialization/copy work, low for harmful magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Templates can be richer, but realistic provider configs are small and no hot high-cardinality workload proves a user-visible regression beyond existing whole-catalog projection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: added work is bounded on mutation paths or a small incremental cost inside an existing whole-catalog projection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use ordinary New Session/model/mode controls and resize the Automation dialog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toolbar construction and responsive layout run while rendering the composer; model configuration work is lazy until queried or changed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A bounded number of toolbar actions and model preference entries per draft; resize cost scales with the small control count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates are synchronous on render/resize; picker model caches retain one model per active scoped surface and release it in a microtask after the last reference.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scoped mode-picker models are keyed by the session observable and disposed after the final release; Automation model preferences are per draft and disposed with it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle and bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM/layout timing is not measured, but there is no loop over large collections or forced read-after-write chain established by the changed hunks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: eager allocations are small, responsive work is bounded, and cache cleanup is explicit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load stored Agent Host Automations after restart and enforce approval policy during active sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Startup maps stored Automation definitions once; permission checks occur at existing runtime decision points.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read existing stored catalog and migrate legacy Copilot mode/approval shapes in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass over N stored Automations at service startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Stored rows were wrapped with run windows without this migration pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds constant-time field checks and only allocates replacement objects for rows requiring migration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of stored Automations N; each row is visited once and unchanged rows retain identity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous one-time startup mapping; no added parallel boundary burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Migration result becomes the in-memory catalog for the process lifetime; no repeated migration per access.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large catalogs increase linear startup work, but per-row work is tiny and no expensive boundary is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded linear startup migration and constant-time policy checks do not establish a meaningful regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 62 changed files and relevant call paths. One medium-confidence-impact, high-mechanism-confidence finding was submitted for repeated serialized provider-capture waits during rapid retargeting. Other new work is bounded, single-shot, lifecycle-cleaned, or piggybacks on pre-existing session/catalog/storage boundaries.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
